newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Lanka awards tender to Glencore, delays second.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka awards tender to Glencore, delays second.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp's (CPC) has awarded one products tender to Swiss trader Glencore and has extended the offer for the second tender to January 10, industry sources said on Friday.

Glencore was awarded the tender to supply 185,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil and 85,000 barrels of 85 to 88-octane leaded gasoline at a premium of $2.10 a barrel and $3.28 a barrel respectively, over spot Singapore quotes.

The company was awarded the cargo as another offer by Singapore-based trader Hin Leong at premiums of $1.86 per barrel and $3.45, for diesel and gasoline respectively, was not "in line with the tender requirements", an industry source said.
Both cargoes were offered on a cost-and-freight basis to Colombo for delivery between January 29-30.
CPC has called for new offers on the second tender, to purchase 185,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel for delivery between January 23-24 to Colombo.
CPC asked for new offers because the best offer from Shell Singapore was outside its requested delivery time.
Shell Singapore offered premiums of $1.63 per barrel and $1.71 to spot Singapore quotes for the sale of 185,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel, respectively.
Both cargoes were offered on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) to Colombo.

Traders said the scheduled 45-day shutdown of the Sapugaskanda 60,000 barrels-per-day refinery from mid-January had led to increased diesel and jet fuel purchases as well as the rare import of a gasoline cargo.
